title: Patch: the account's player statistics keep only real cards and whole counts, so the public stats page never shows text a player made up
thread:
**Issue #1771 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #1771: Patch: the account's player statistics keep only real cards and whole counts, so the public stats page never shows text a player made up
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The public statistics page lists players with their games, win rate and favourite card, and anyone can read it without signing in. Today the server keeps whatever a player's browser sends it about their statistics, so someone who sends a hand-made request can make the "Favourite card" column show any words they like, up to a long paragraph, and none of it passes the word filter that chat messages and usernames go through. Once this is built, the server keeps only the counts the page reads, for cards that exist, and drops everything else, so the column only ever names a real card.

## Why
- `PUT /api/stats/player` (`crates/server/src/api/stats.rs`, `put_player`, around lines 1108-1137) stores the body's `stats` object as it came: `Some(Value::Object(map)) => map.iter().map(|(key, value)| (key.clone(), value.clone())).collect()`. Its only check is the size cap `PLAYER_STATS_BYTES_MAX` (65,536).
- The public summary (`crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`, `to_public_player_summary`, around 3088-3101, which both stores use) turns every key under `cards` with a positive `played` into a favourite card: `played_counts.push(FavouriteCard { id: id.clone(), count: played })`.
- The players tab prints an id the catalog does not hold as it is (`apps/web/src/routes/stats.tsx:1267`: `favCardDef ? readerName(favCardDef) : topCard.id`), and `GET /api/stats/players` needs no session. React escapes it, so this is not script injection, but it is unmoderated public text.
- R1142000 says the account copy holds the summary's inputs only: the four totals, and for each card `played`, `playedAgainst`, `destroyed` and `defeated`. Only the client's `syncPayload` (`apps/web/src/stats/sync.ts`) holds to that. The server never checks it.
- Every other player-written text another player sees is filtered: chat through `mask_blocked_words` (`crates/server/src/social/chat.rs:177`) and usernames through R1433's filter (`crates/server/src/username/mod.rs`).

## Proposal
In `put_player`, build the stored copy in R1142000's shape before `player_stats_put`:
- `games`, `wins`, `losses` and `draws` are kept when each is a whole number of 0 or more, and dropped otherwise.
- `cards` keeps only ids in the server's catalog (`app.catalog.defs`), each holding only the four counters as positive whole numbers. An entry left with none is dropped, as `syncPayload` drops it.
- Every other key is dropped.

The answer echoes the stored copy, as it does today. A fused or crafted card's generated id and a custom card's id are dropped with the rest, since they name no card the page can show. Amend R1142000, or add a note in this issue's block, to say the server holds the copy to that shape, list the proving test in `proven_in`, and run `cargo jackioh spec index`.

Out of scope: the counts themselves stay the client's to report, as R654 decides.

## Where it lands
- `crates/server/src/api/stats.rs` (`put_player`)
- `crates/server/tests/api/stats.rs`
- `spec/rulings/R1142000.md` (or a new note) and `spec/INDEX.md`; SPEC §9.11

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A PUT carrying a `cards` key that is no catalog id, a counter that is a string, a negative or fractional counter and an unknown top-level key stores none of them; `GET /api/stats/player` and `GET /api/stats/players` show only the catalog card and the valid counts.
- [ ] A PUT of what `syncPayload` sends today is stored unchanged, and the existing R1142000 and R654 tests stay green.
- [ ] The new test is named for the ruling (`fn r1142000_…` or the new id), and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] No store or migration change; `cargo test -p jackioh-server` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` are green.

## Size and risks
Small: one function (about 40 lines), one test and the ruling sentence. Medium, because of the ruling. A client build that sent an extra field loses only that field, which nothing reads. Rows already stored keep their junk until that player's next sync; a one-off cleanup is not proposed, since it would be a migration.
```
